items.title: Workflow SDK 5: built for production
items.summary: When we first launched Workflow SDK, the goal was simple: write regular async JavaScript, and let the SDK keep it running through crashes, deployments, and long waits.Last year, , with the world-class developer experience Vercel is known for. Then we watched what our customers built with it.we shipped just thatMore than 4 billion steps and 700 million runs later, two clear patterns have emerged. As those workloads matured, Workflow matured with them. Our priorities have always been security, reliability, and performance. Here’s how Workflow SDK 5 delivers on all three.The Workflow  stores step arguments and return values so a run can recover after a crash or deployment. That data can include sensitive customer information, model context, credentials, and tool-call results. Persisting it requires strong protection.event logWorkflow SDK , before it leaves your code. Workflow and step inputs and outputs, hook payloads, and stream data are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, using a unique key for each run. With encryption enabled, any Workflow SDK backend, including Vercel, only sees and stores ciphertext. Plaintext is decrypted in your deployment or in authorized observability tools.encrypts every payload end to endOn Vercel, encryption needs no setup and no code changes. Each run’s key is derived from a key scoped to the deployment that created it, so a run can only decrypt its own data. Your workflow code doesn’t change:Because Vercel manages the keys by default, observability keeps working. Names, timings, and statuses are always visible, and when you need to see a payload, you can decrypt it in the dashboard or the CLI. Decryption happens in your browser or terminal, follows the same permissions as the project’s environment variables, and every request is recorded in your team’s audit log.Encryption is implemented in the SDK, so it can also protect payloads on  before they reach storage, queues, or streams.self-hosted WorldsA  by implementing  with your . Return the same 32-byte key for each run on every call so the SDK can encrypt new payloads and decrypt them during replay:custom World enables encryptionkey managementgetEncryptionKeyForRun()Cross-run writes are sealed too. When code resumes another run’s hook, starts a run in another deployment, or writes into a stream forwarded from another run, the payload is encrypted to the target run’s public key. The writer can encrypt for that run without reading its existing payloads.You can also limit how long sensitive data is stored. With  set to , inputs, outputs, and stream contents are deleted as soon as a run completes or fails. The run’s metadata stays visible in observability.payload retentionexperimental_retention: 0The  makes runs easier to navigate, with span search, zoom, a minimap, and local inspection during development.redesigned trace viewer are new in v5. They let you attach searchable context to a run, such as an order ID, and then find runs by it. Attributes are plaintext, so they should not contain secrets.Run attributesIn Workflow SDK 4, every run lived in . Even when a project was deployed to several regions, each run’s event log, queue, and streams were only stored in one region, so a step running anywhere else made cross-region requests to record its progress.iad1For v5, we . Each run has its own home region: its state, queue dispatch, and streams are served from the region where it started, without cross-region round trips on the hot path.deployed Workflow infrastructure to every Vercel Function regionBy default, a run starts in the region of the function that starts it. Deploy to several regions, and each run stays close to the user who triggered it, with no configuration:To place a run somewhere else, . That lets a workflow run next to the database it reads and writes, or keep a customer’s data in the region where it has to stay:pass a region to start()The  option decides where a run’s data lives. Your steps run where your app is deployed, so deploy to that region too if you want them to execute there. Existing v4 runs stay in .regioniad1Regional isolation also improves reliability. A disruption in one region does not have to stop new runs in healthy regions. For projects with  configured, steps can execute in a fallback region while continuing to use the run’s original home region for state. That state remains pinned to its home region; it does not migrate during failover.Vercel Function failoverWith the help of anonymized telemetry and close collaboration with many customers, we found and fixed dozens of rare bugs and race conditions in the Workflow runtime. Workflow SDK also recovers on its own from more kinds of intermittent network errors.As a result, with Workflow SDK 5, we’ve seen almost no runs fail or stall because of a platform or runtime bug.In Workflow SDK 4, every step invocation involved a queue hop to start the step and another to continue the workflow.
